audit.account:
Question: is the Ta coordination the same locally as on average? Answer: yes, within the resolution of this PDF. The Ta–Se distances agree across r to about 0.02 Å and show no drift with r.

Method: I followed the pdf-workflow stages. The long-range baseline (20–30 Å, the data end at 30 Å) refined scale, cell, the isotropic-equivalent U of each site, then the average positions; it converged at 9.34 % (4.09 %), with Ta1's average position shift at the esd level. Qdamp and Qbroad were held at their loaded values throughout; I did not check them against a standard. Correlated motion (2–20 Å) refined δ2 alone to 1.53956 with the scale and cell free; 9.34 % on that window was 9.31 %. For the local fit (2–10 Å), I held the cell and δ2 and freed the scale and positions; the positions moved by less than 0.0002 in fractional units, and Rw was 11.33 %.

The boxcar scan (2–20 Å, 4 Å boxes, step 2 Å, scale and positions free, Ta1 bonds reported per box) gives Ta1–Se2 ×3 between 2.503 and 2.525 Å and Ta1–Se1 ×3 between 2.756 and 2.769 Å, with no monotonic drift. The high-r boxes (average region) give Ta1–Se2 2.5136 Å and Ta1–Se1 2.7640 Å. The box-to-box scatter (about 0.01–0.02 Å) is the same size as any local difference, so the scan shows no local Ta distortion distinct from the average. The Se2 position drifts by about 4 esd across r, but this changes the Ta–Se2 length by only about 0.01 Å and not monotonically, so I do not read it as a local distortion. The lowest-r box (2–6 Å) has a high Rw of 17.3 % against about 5 % elsewhere. I attribute this to near-neighbour misfit (the correlated-motion treatment) rather than to a resolved Ta environment, but I did not test that directly.

Caveats: the esds on PDF parameters are not statistical, and the bond lengths carry no esds, so the no-difference conclusion rests on the box-to-box spread, not on a formal test. δ2 was chosen as the correlated-motion term for a 299 K sample (δ1 is the alternative at high temperature) and was not compared with δ1. The occupancy and particle-size stages were not run, since the question did not call for them. If the local-versus-average question needs a firmer answer, a posterior on the Ta–Se2 length (bayesian-check) and a δ1 comparison would be the next steps.

Ta local vs average (GaTa4Se8, 299 K X-ray PDF): boxcar 2–20 Å, width 4 Å. Ta–Se2 ×3 stays 2.503–2.525 Å and Ta–Se1 ×3 2.756–2.769 Å across boxes, with no monotonic drift; average model gives 2.520 and 2.768 Å. Lowest-r box (2–6 Å) has Rw 17.3% vs about 5% elsewhere; attributed to near-neighbour misfit, not resolved. δ2 chosen for 299 K (δ1 not tested).

Question: is the Ta coordination the same locally as on average in GaTa4Se8 (299 K X-ray PDF)? Answer: the coordination is the same; the Ta–Se bond lengths agree to about 0.01 Å across all windows.

Approach, following the PDF method: the long-range baseline first (20–30 Å: scale, cell, isotropic site B's and the positions free; converged at Rw 11.73 % on that window, nothing at a bound). Then one correlated-motion term, δ2 = 1.65965, over 2–20 Å. δ2 rather than δ1 is the general-practice choice at low temperature; at 299 K that is a judgment call, and it does not change the coordination result. Then the local stage on 2–10 Å with the positions free, and a boxcar scan (free set: scale and the three positions) read as Ta–Se bond lengths box by box.

Result. Ta sits in 3 Se2 and 3 Se1 in every box, so the 3+3 coordination is the same locally as on average. Across the 4–10 Å boxes the Ta–Se2 bond is 2.5140 to 2.5142 Å and the Ta–Se1 bond 2.7573 to 2.7625 Å. The 2–6 Å box gives bonds within about 0.02 Å of these. Over the 20–30 Å baseline the Ta–Se2 bond is about 0.01 Å longer than in the 4–10 Å boxes, comparable to the box-to-box scatter, so I do not claim a local distortion from it. The lowest box (2–6 Å) is not trusted: its Rw is 18.03 %, against about 5 % in the boxes at higher r. The position drifts across the boxes reach about 4.5 esds (Se2), but PDF esds are not statistical and understate the uncertainty.

Caveats. The PDF esds are not statistical, and the bond lengths carry no esds. The 0.01 Å difference is not tested with a posterior; if it matters, sample_posterior on the Ta–Se2 bond is the next step. The low-r fit (2–6 Å, Rw 18 %) is the weak point and is left open. ADPs were held isotropic, and Qdamp and Qbroad were held at their starting values (no standard was loaded). The occupancy and particle-size stages were not run; neither was needed for this question.

Baseline (20–30 Å window, scale+cell+site B+positions free, isotropic U): Rw 4.53 %, converged, nothing at a bound. Long-range average structure is the reference for the local comparison.

PDF local-vs-average (GaTa4Se8, 299 K). Baseline 20–30 Å: Rw 4.53, Ta–Se2 2.525 Å ×3, Ta–Se1 2.768 Å ×3. Boxcar 4–10 Å boxes: Ta–Se2 2.514, Ta–Se1 2.757–2.763. 2–6 Å box Rw 18 %, not trusted. Coordination 3+3 in every box.

Question: is the Ta coordination in GaTa4Se8 (299 K, F-43m) the same locally as on average? Within the cubic model, yes. The local fit shows a residual misfit that the cubic group cannot absorb, so a small local distortion is not excluded.

Method: I followed the pdf-workflow, with Qdamp and Qbroad held at their preset values (no standard was loaded to check them against). Baseline at 15–30 Å (the data end at 30 Å): scale and cell, then one isotropic U per site, then the three constrained positions. Rw fell from 5.29 to 4.93 to 4.76 over these three steps. The position shifts at long range are about 1e-4 or smaller, so the average structure is essentially the starting one. Correlated motion: δ1 refined with the scale at 2–20 Å, with Rw 10.42 % at the end of the later local fits. Local fit at 2–10 Å: cell and δ1 held, scale and positions free. Rw was 11.56. Freeing the ADPs a little afterwards gave 10.42.

Ta coordination: average, long-range fit: Ta–Se2 2.52 Å ×3, Ta–Se1 2.77 Å ×3, Ta–Ta 3.00 Å (the Ta4 cluster edge). Local fit (2–10 Å): Ta–Se2 2.52 Å, Ta–Se1 2.77 Å, Ta–Ta 3.00 Å. Boxcar scan (6 Å wide boxes, 2 Å step, up and down in agreement): Ta–Se2 2.5217 → 2.5160 Å and Ta–Se1 2.7662 → 2.7599 Å from the 2–8 Å box to the 4–10 Å box. This is a drift of about 0.006 Å. It is small against the 0.25 Å difference between the two Ta–Se bond types and comparable to the box-to-box scatter, so I do not read it as a distortion. The Ta ADP barely moved from the baseline (0.558 → 0.576 Å²).

Caveats and open issue: Rw is not low in the local range, with 12.1 % in the 2–8 Å box against 5.5 % in the 4–10 Å box. The misfit therefore lives at the shortest distances, and it is not removed by the Ta positions or the ADPs allowed by F-43m. I cannot inspect the difference curve in real space with these tools, so I cannot say which peaks are responsible. A local symmetry-lowering distortion of the Ta4 clusters (for example a trigonal R3m-type one, as in the low-temperature phase) would show up this way, but so would an imperfect δ1 or Qdamp/Qbroad. The esds are not statistical and the G(r) points are correlated. I did not run a posterior check, because no single value carries a distortion claim. Next step, if you want it: lower the symmetry with list_subgroups and lower_symmetry and test a Ta4 cluster distortion. I did not do this because the method leaves the symmetry decision to you.

Question: is the Ta coordination (distorted TaSe6 octahedron, Ta–Ta in the Ta4 cluster) the same locally as on average in cubic F-43m GaTa4Se8 at 299 K? Following the PDF method: baseline on 20–30 Å (the data end at 30; scale, cell, then U, then positions; Qdamp and Qbroad held, no standard was loaded to refine them against), Rw 14.91 % at the last step. Then 2–20 Å with scale and δ1 (high-T term), then a local fit on 2–10 Å with positions free, then boxcar scans (5 Å and 3 Å boxes) reporting the Ta1 bond lengths box by box.

Result, lengths: the mean Ta coordination is the same locally as on average. Boxcar Ta–Se lengths (3×Se2 near 2.52 Å, 3×Se1 near 2.76 Å) move by about 0.01 Å or less between the low-r and high-r boxes. The intra-cluster Ta–Ta is about 3.00 Å in the average model. Refined positions stay within about 1e-3 of the average model's, which is not a distortion of the first shell in the cubic group.

Result, fit quality: the local fit is not good. Rw is about 13.5% in the 2–7 Å box and 21% in the 2–5 Å box, against about 5% at 5–9.5 Å and about 4% on the baseline window. Neither free positions nor δ1 lowers it on 2–6 Å. Freeing the ADPs does (18.5% to 14.9%), and the Ta U sum rises to about 0.013 from about 0.007 at the start. That points to local displacements or disorder the cubic model absorbs into larger, anisotropic U, not to a shift of the mean bond lengths. The most that can be said is that the short-range structure is more disordered than the average model describes (an off-centre or cluster distortion is plausible, not demonstrated).

Caveats: PDF esds are not statistical, and the boxcar has only 2–4 boxes. Qdamp and Qbroad are the file's values and were not checked against a standard. Whether a lower-symmetry (e.g. rhombohedral) model fits the 2–6 Å range better is the next step. It is not done here and is your decision (list_subgroups / lower_symmetry).
